A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PDFNet research. Their text, equations, tables and figures are readable, including v4's supplementary material. V5 has no separate appendix, but retained content can be reliably matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V4 reports original PDFNet experiments on DIS-5K, component and loss ablations, and HRSOD/UHRSD results in supplementary Table 9.

after.justification: V5 retains original DIS-5K and HRSOD/UHRSD results and ablations, and reports additional depth-generator evaluations in Table 7.

M1.justification: The shared encoder, 64-patch branch, FSE/CoA modules, depth-refinement decoder and training losses remain unchanged in Figures 3–4 and Equations 1–22. The expanded PDFNet name and additional depth-generator tests do not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use DIS-5K, HRSOD and UHRSD. The HRSOD experiments move from v4's supplementary material to v5 Section 4.5 and Table 6. Additional depth generators are model configurations within retained data and tasks, rather than new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V5 removes RISNet, DACOD and FP-DIS rows from Table 1, although FP-DIS remains named in its caption. The SAM, HQ-SAM and Pi-SAM comparison in v4 Table 10 disappears. The loss-transfer comparison replaces DACOD with CPNet, while the HRSOD comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: V5 expands generator-substitution testing and changes parameter accounting to include external depth estimators and diffusion VAEs. Its stated augmentation list omits random cropping, without establishing that cropping was removed from implementation. Data splits, input resolution, optimizer, batch size and DIS/HRSOD training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V5 retains component, loss and patch-count ablations and expands depth-generator robustness testing beyond DAM-v2 to DAM-Small and DepthPro. However, it removes the loss-weight case study, the quantitative pre-metric binarization experiment in v4 Table 8, and the failure-case analysis in supplementary Section 9 and Figure 12.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for the performance comparisons. Figure 1 retains the depth-variance distribution analysis. The added results introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Reported evidence changes substantially through removal of foundation-model, binarization and baseline result sets. New DIS-VD results include Fmax-beta 0.904 with DAM-Small and 0.917 with DepthPro; CPNet's loss-transfer comparison reports 0.892 without versus 0.895 with the loss. Retained Table 1 scores, all PDFNet-S/B/L scores and HRSOD scores are unchanged after matching relocated tables.

T1.justification: V5 Section 3.3 adds the explicit boundedness-based justification that diff lies in [0,1], making the depth-stability loss nonnegative. This is a limited mathematical qualification; the loss definitions and Equations 1–22 otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central efficiency claim is substantially narrowed: v4 emphasizes 94M parameters and less than 11% of diffusion-model parameters or computational cost; v5 includes DAM-v2 and claims less than 50% of parameters. V5 also explicitly claims the first incorporation of depth as a DIS modality and elevates DIS/HRSOD generalization into the conclusion.

C2.justification: Core depth-loss and patch-density interpretations remain. V5 adds an explanation connecting background depth variance to disconnected surfaces and extends the robustness interpretation to other generators. It removes the explicit limitations concerning ultra-fine details and monocular-depth errors, together with suggested remedies. The binarization qualification survives in Table 1's caption.

D1.justification: V5 newly states that comparator evaluations use official model parameters and were rerun on an RTX 4090, and explains inference-time auxiliary parameter accounting. The code-access pointer changes from a direct repository link to a project website. V4's explicit PyTorch declaration and default-Large reporting convention are omitted; most implementation details remain.

R1.justification: V5 distinguishes DIS from saliency-focused HRSOD and explicitly positions depth incorporation as a first for DIS. It adds references including Segment Any Motion in Videos and Source-free Depth for Object Pop-out, while removing SAM-family and RGB-D COD references. The central positioning against non-diffusion and diffusion approaches remains.

P1.justification: V5 substantially reorganizes the narrative, rewrites the abstract and introduction, expands the conclusion, and introduces numbered section hierarchies. Selected supplementary content becomes main-text material under ablation and generalizability sections, while the separate supplement disappears. Author-date citations become numerical, and PDFNet's expanded name changes.

P2.justification: Table 1 replaces the backbone column with modality, reorganizes comparison groups and incorporates previously supplementary PDFNet variants. Other retained tables move into compact main-text layouts. Qualitative panels are reduced and rearranged, including Figures 1, 5 and the loss comparison; several supplementary figures, including the CoA schematic and failure panels, are removed.

improvement.justification: V5 improves transparency by correcting the headline parameter accounting and placing the existing binarization caveat beside Table 1; additional depth-generator tests also strengthen robustness evidence. However, it removes the supporting binarization experiment, explicit failure conditions and substantial comparison evidence. With the core method and principal scores unchanged, these gains compete with losses in auditability and limitations disclosure, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
